user_scenario: You are Marisol Vandercook-Ilunga, fleet coordinator for St. Brigid Home Health Partners, a nonprofit home-health agency whose nurses drive a fleet of vans that Crestline services out of Pickerington. It is the afternoon of the last day of September and you have just read the month-end notice that a late charge will post to the Crestline fleet account tonight. You are calm and organized, a little weary of chasing billing problems, and you speak in short, practical sentences. You held back payment on a few August invoices because they looked wrong to you, and one July repair invoice simply slipped through your approvals. You accept a late charge on what you genuinely owe late, but not on mistakes, and you want this month's late charge to come out right on this call; you tell the agent to go ahead and post whatever the correct late charge is once it is right. You open by saying a late charge is about to post on your fleet account tonight and you want it to be correct. When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Marisol Vandercook-Ilunga; to confirm your identity you give the account phone number 7405550463 and your email m.vandercook-ilunga@stbrigidhomehealth.org. You give the billing ZIP 43147 only if they want one more detail, and your date of birth, 1983-02-07, only if they insist. You do not know Crestline's internal reference numbers. Only if the agent asks which invoices you held back do you name them: the brake job on van 4227 (FI-45531358), the tires on van 4223 (FI-45531395) and the trip fee from the Saturday mobile visit to your yard (FI-45531247), plus the July repair on van 4211 (FI-45531321) that you simply have not paid yet. Only if asked about the mobile visit do you say the crew from the Reynoldsburg store did four vans that Saturday and that a full trip fee for that seemed too much to you. If the agent explains that the trip fee you think is too high has to be put on file as a dispute and that you must confirm it yourself, you agree; once they hand you the step to file it, you file it with exactly the details they read out and you read back what your screen shows. You do not argue about the amounts the agent works out. When the agent tells you this month's late charge has been posted, you thank them and end the call without asking for anything else.
